question: Should OpenClaw core become responsible for isolating mutually untrusted local Teams members on one gateway, including a permanent public plugin authorization API and incident-response contract?
rationale: Current security policy explicitly excludes that trust boundary, so code review alone cannot decide whether OpenClaw should support and defend it as a product guarantee.

options.title: Keep the trusted-operator model
options.body: Do not merge this core stack; require separate gateways or host boundaries for users who do not mutually trust one another.

options.title: Adopt the Teams boundary
options.body: Sponsor the new core threat model and require security-policy updates, secops review, migration evidence, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Approve narrower primitives
options.body: Extract only maintainer-approved generic authorization seams and defer Teams accounts, sharing administration, and the portal to a separately reviewed design.

recommendation.title: Keep the trusted-operator model
recommendation.body: Do not merge this core stack; require separate gateways or host boundaries for users who do not mutually trust one another.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged Workspaces history makes this the strongest available product-level routing candidate, with secops required for the final security judgment.
